explanation: The roots are where the parabola crosses the x-axis (y = 0). The discriminant b² − 4ac (the part under the square root) tells you how many real roots there are BEFORE you solve: positive -> two, zero -> one (the vertex touches the axis), negative -> none (it floats above or below). Watch the green roots appear and merge as you change c.
bullets: Roots are the x-intercepts: where ax² + bx + c = 0.
Discriminant b² − 4ac: >0 two roots, =0 one, <0 none (real).
The two roots are symmetric about the axis x = −b/2a.
